blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Engagement is not the same as happiness. Happy employees are not always productive, and highly engaged employees are not always smiling. Engagement is about commitment, energy and a real connection between the person and the work.

Most companies run annual engagement surveys with long questionnaires. The problem is that the results arrive months after the issues appeared. Today, many HR teams prefer pulse surveys — short, frequent check-ins that help them pick up early signals before small problems become crises.

The real test is not running the survey. It is what the company does afterwards. If employees take time to share feedback and nothing changes, engagement drops even further. The leaders must follow up, explain their decisions and show real actions.

items.q: According to the text, what is engagement really about?
options: Commitment, energy and connection to the work
items.why: "Engagement is about commitment, energy and a real connection between the person and the work."

items.q: What problem does the text mention with annual engagement surveys?
options: The results arrive months after the issues appeared
items.why: "the results arrive months after the issues appeared."

items.q: Why do many HR teams prefer pulse surveys?
options: They help pick up early signals
items.why: "short, frequent check-ins that help them pick up early signals."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Running the survey is the most important step.
Feedback without action can lower engagement.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o teste real não é rodar a pesquisa, mas o que se faz depois.

items.q: What does the text suggest happens when employees give feedback and nothing changes?
items.why: Inferência apoiada no texto: "If employees take time to share feedback and nothing changes, engagement drops even further."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando os resultados da pesquisa rápida. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for joining. I want to keep this short and practical, because the whole point of a pulse survey is speed.

The headline is that engagement dropped off in two teams this quarter — Operations and Client Services. The scores aren't a disaster, but they've moved in the wrong direction for two check-ins in a row, and that pattern is what worries me. What I'm picking up on, reading the comments, is not pay. It's workload. Several people mentioned late nights and cancelled holidays, which to me is an early signal of burnout.

Now, here's the part that matters. Last year we asked, people answered honestly, and then almost nothing happened. I don't want to repeat that. If we run another survey and don't act on it, we'll do more harm than saying nothing at all.

So I'm not asking you to solve everything today. I'm asking each of you to commit to one visible action this month and to follow through on it. One change people can actually see. That's how we start building a listening culture — one response at a time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Which two teams saw engagement drop off, according to Emily?
items.why: "engagement dropped off in two teams this quarter — Operations and Client Services."

items.q: What does Emily say the comments are really about?
items.why: "It's not pay. It's workload." — ela cita noites em claro e férias canceladas.

items.q: Why is Emily worried about the numbers specifically?
options: They have moved down for two check-ins in a row
The scores are the lowest ever recorded
Only one person answered the survey
items.why: "they've moved in the wrong direction for two check-ins in a row, and that pattern is what worries me."

items.q: What does Emily imply about running a survey and then doing nothing?
options: It has no effect on engagement
It can be worse than saying nothing at all
It is better than not asking at all
items.why: Inferência: "we'll do more harm than saying nothing at all" — pedir e não agir corrói a confiança.

items.q: What is Emily mainly asking the leaders to do?
options: Commit to one visible action and follow through on it
Solve every problem before the end of the day
items.why: "commit to one visible action this month and to follow through on it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We run a pulse survey every month instead of one long questionnaire a year." A pulse survey is…
options: a short, frequent check-in with employees
items.why: Pulse survey = pesquisa rápida e frequente, para captar sinais cedo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Engagement is about ___ , not just being happy at work."
items.why: Commitment = comprometimento, o núcleo da definição de engajamento na lição.

items.q: "Long hours and cancelled holidays are an early signal of trouble." An early signal is…
items.why: Early signal = sinal precoce, que aparece antes de o problema virar crise.

items.q: "Six months of overwork pushed two of my best people into burnout." Burnout is…
options: a state of exhaustion from prolonged stress
items.why: Burnout = esgotamento causado por estresse prolongado no trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "We are trying to build a ___ , where people feel their feedback is actually heard."
items.why: Listening culture = cultura de escuta, construída resposta a resposta.

blocks.instruction: Phrasal verbs e expressões que aparecem ao falar de engajamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Reading the comments, I started to pick up on a pattern." To pick up on means to…
items.why: Pick up on = perceber, captar algo que não estava explícito.

items.q: "There's no point asking if we don't act on the results." To act on means to…
items.why: Act on = agir sobre, tomar providências a partir de algo.

items.q: "The team agreed on a plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Engagement scores dropped off in two teams last quarter." To drop off means to…
items.why: Drop off = cair, diminuir (aqui, os índices de engajamento).

items.q: "After the survey, leaders must follow up with the teams." To follow up means to…
options: take further action or check back
items.why: Follow up = dar seguimento, retomar o contato para tratar do que foi levantado.
